text.1: This tutorial teaches the basics of Galactica. The User’s Manual also explains advanced play and strategy. You can close the tutorial at any time to return to your previous game.
text.2: Choose New game from the command menu to open game setup.
text.3: The supplied settings are suitable for this practice game. Click Start to accept them.
text.4: Enter your player name, then click Start below the name field.
text.5: Most play takes place on this map. Galactica is turn based: take as much time as you need to plan your moves before ending each turn.
text.6: The grid is the starmap. Andromeda is your home system, shown in your player color. Its pulsing selection marker shows which object is selected.
text.7: Pan with the scrollbars, Alt/Option-drag or middle-button drag. Zoom with the mouse wheel or + and −. Try changing the zoom; the tutorial continues after a short pause.
text.8: The system information window controls the effort devoted to population growth, shipbuilding and research. More colonies provide more resources for your empire.
text.9: The construction bar shows the selected hull and its progress. Your colony ship is almost 99% complete, so it should finish next turn. A hull is complete at 100%.
text.10: Reduce shipbuilding effort a little with the Ships slider. Click or drag in its bar to set a target level; the colony ship is close enough to finish anyway.
text.11: The solid slider fill shows actual production; the vertical marker shows your target. Actual levels take several turns to adjust. Lock icons hold target allocations while other targets change.
text.12: Orders and production take effect when the turn ends. Click End turn, or press Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, to process this turn.
text.13: Congratulations on your first colony ship! Important reports appear at the start of a turn and remain in Events. Press Enter or Escape to acknowledge this report.
text.14: Your opponents have been busy too. Acknowledge any remaining reports with Enter or Escape. Then press Tab or click Next item to review the next item needing attention.
text.15: Use your new colony ship to establish another colony. Colonization increases the resources available for building your empire and its ships.
text.16: With the colony ship selected, click Orders to begin setting a destination. In its Course window you can also use Add or A to add a waypoint.
text.17: The tracking line shows the course you are choosing. Click the star S-20 to set the colony ship’s destination.
text.18: That was not S-20. Click Retry, then choose S-20 as the destination.
text.19: Build a defense satellite to protect your homeworld. Select Andromeda and click Defense in its building controls.
text.20: Restore equal production targets so the satellite builds promptly. Click the = icon beside the sliders, or press =. Unlock any allocation you want to equalize.
text.21: Your orders are ready. Click End turn or press Cmd/Ctrl+Enter.
text.22: The colony ship is moving toward S-20 and should arrive next turn. Its motion vector shows the next leg of travel. End the turn again.
text.23: Defense satellites remain at their building system and are always on patrol. Your new satellite protects Andromeda. Press Enter or Escape to acknowledge its report.
text.24: You have a new colony! A colony ship automatically colonizes an unoccupied system on arrival, then remains available for further orders.
text.25: Give the new colony a name. Select it, click Rename or press N, and accept the name New Terra.
text.26: New Terra’s production levels are fine for now. Switch its building controls to Battleship; it does not need a satellite yet.
text.27: Good! Press Tab or click Next item to check for more events.
text.28: Ships request orders after finishing a course or spending too long idle. Send the same colony ship to S-7 to establish another colony.
text.29: Press Tab or click Next item again to check for more events.
text.30: The clunk indicates there is nothing more needing attention. Before ending the turn, select Andromeda.
text.31: Research has raised Andromeda’s technology. Switch it to building a Scout: this fast, unarmed courier will distribute technology to your colonies.
text.32: The protective ring around Andromeda indicates its patrolling satellite. End the turn to continue.
text.33: Scouts are fast, unarmed couriers. They alone can pick up higher system technology and carry it to other colonies. Press Enter or Escape to acknowledge this report.
text.34: Your Scout is ready for orders. Send it to New Terra to deliver Andromeda’s latest technology.
text.35: Excellent! Press Tab or click Next item.
text.36: Build a fleet to attack your opponents. Andromeda and New Terra should both produce battleships. Start by selecting Andromeda.
text.38: New battleships can assemble into a fleet at a rendezvous point. Click the map’s Rendezvous button, or press U, to begin placing one.
text.39: Place the rendezvous point in space between Andromeda and New Terra. Click the map inside that region; it need not be on a star.
text.40: Name your new rendezvous point Alpha and accept the name.
text.41: Select Andromeda. Beside Send to, click Set, then click rendezvous point Alpha to make it the automatic destination for new ships.
text.42: Select New Terra and use Set beside Send to to give its new ships the same destination, Alpha.
text.43: Both colonies will now send new battleships to Alpha, where they assemble into a fleet. End the turn.
text.44: A Scout delivers its technology to a lower-tech allied system and picks up higher technology for later delivery. Send it toward S-7, then press Tab or click Next item.
text.45: There is no more attention to handle. End the turn.
text.46: A lot happened this turn. Press Tab or click Next item to review it.
text.47: Another colony is established. Leave its production as it is for now and press Tab or click Next item.
text.48: S-35 would be a useful next colony, but let us practice defense first. With the colony ship selected, press P or choose Patrol to guard S-7.
text.49: Your colony ship patrols S-7. Patrolling ships ambush attackers and coordinate with planetary defenses for a defensive advantage. Press Tab or click Next item.
text.50: Compare your progress with the other players. Open Compare Players from the command menu.
text.51: The highlighted best and worst values identify category leaders and laggards. Close Compare Players when you have finished reviewing it.
text.53: Your Scout has arrived at S-7 to deliver technology. Leave it without new orders for now and press Tab or click Next item.
text.54: There is nothing more needing attention. End the turn.
text.55: Traveler is the first battleship drive class. Higher technology unlocks stronger, faster classes. Press Enter or Escape to acknowledge this report.
text.56: The automatic destinations are paying off: ships from both colonies are gathering at Alpha. Further ships will join while the fleet remains there.
text.57: Open Exchange ships for the selected fleet to examine its members.
text.58: The fleet contains the two new Travelers. Select a member and use Exchange to move it out; the same window can move ships between groups at a shared location.
text.59: Health bars show ship damage. Green means healthy; more red means more damage. Destroyed ships are lost. Let damaged mobile ships rest at an allied system to repair; patrolling ships do not repair.
text.60: That completes the tutorial! The practice game stays open so you can keep playing. Read the User’s Manual for strategy, and put your colony ship at S-7 back to work. Previous games remain in Open games.
text.100: Your current game will be hidden while the tutorial runs. Cancellation returns to it; after finishing, you can select it from Open games. Close the tutorial if you prefer to keep playing it now.
text.101: Close the current dialog before starting the tutorial, then click OK to try again. Closing the tutorial cancels it without replacing your game.
text.103: Hosting is a multiplayer option. This tutorial uses a local single-player game. Cancel hosting and return to local game setup to continue.
